thread:
nina: Quick decision thread  Dedicated GA readiness. I want to lock the launch path and a minimal burst model so sales/legal can start talking to pilots. High-level options: 1) nano-first (small default pools + optional burst addon), 2) standard-first (larger default pools, conservative burst). Need a call today on which to commit to for the GA roadmap.

raj: Nano-first favoured from infra: smaller pools reduce risk and let us tune autoscale knobs. Ops caveat: need stronger admission control to avoid noisy neighbors on shared infra during burst windows.

clare: From CS/pilot feedback customers prefer predictable behavior over raw headroom. They'll sign up for a paid "burst credit" if the contract is clear. Also ask for an easy way to opt into prewarm for low-latency use cases.

drew: Legal flavour: we can provide a "burst credit allowance" clause. Proposed wording: "Customer will receive a configurable burst credit balance (X tokens/minute for Y minutes). Exceeding the allowance will incur overage at the published burst rate. Burst credits are not guaranteed during force‑major events." Keep it short and carve out maint windows.

sanjay: Pricing suggests two flavours: (A) burst-addon (metered, pay-as-you-go) and (B) commit-with-headroom (higher monthly commit, included headroom). We should prepare example pricing tiers for both.

nina: Operational gating: what telemetry and thresholds do we need to gate GA? Propose these minimal signals: p99 latency, 1-minute burst_success %, KV cache hit-rate, prewarm recovery time. Thoughts?

raj: Agree. Add autoscale stability metric (scaling events per 5m). Also add a boolean flag in telemetry for quantization_mode used (q4_0/q5_0) so we can correlate quality impact. Example autoscale profile to start with:

```
{
  "min_replicas": 1,
  "target_rps": 40,
  "scale_up_window_sec": 30,
  "scale_down_window_sec": 120,
  "burst_headroom": {
    "enabled": true,
    "percent": 100,
    "duration_sec": 300
  }
}
```

clare: Add rollback conditions: if burst_success < 98% for any 1-minute window sustained for 5 minutes OR +25% p99 vs baseline for >10 minutes then pause rollouts and open an incident. Also require a customer opt-out flow.

drew: For contracts we should avoid absolute guarantees. Use soft language + explicit overage pricing and an escape clause for emergency throttles. I'll draft a one-paragraph template.

sanjay: I'll mock pricing buckets and show profitability at 2x and 3x burst multipliers. Will attach spreadsheet.

telemetry-bot: canary-deploy created: pool=nano-canary-2, artifact=inference-runtime@2025.02.7, started=2025-01-09T11:12:03Z

nina: On quality: we must gate quantization flips. If q4_0 is used we need a quality delta threshold < 0.8% BLEU/semantic-drop on the pilot eval set. marco is out this week so tradeoff analysis will be sticky.

raj: We'll add a runtime flag to disable quantization per-tenant so pilots can opt into it. Also plan to emit a "burst_reject" event with reason codes so product can report transparent failures to customers.

clare: Customer onboarding checklist: 1) sign burst addendum, 2) opt into prewarm if needed, 3) provide SLA contact for oncall, 4) agree pilot success criteria (we'll use product's telemetry).

nina: Proposed rollout: internal dogfood -> 10 invited pilots (opt-in) -> 50 beta customers -> GA. Gate GA on: successful pilot (no rollbacks), metrics within threshold for 72h, pricing tiers published, legal template approved.

raj: Ops action: implement burst_reject telemetry, per-tenant quantization opt-out, and autoscale profile defaults. ETA 2 weeks.

drew: Legal will circulate the burst addendum draft tomorrow AM.

sanjay: Pricing buckets ready by EOD tomorrow.

nina: Great. Action list captured: (1) raj: infra tickets for telemetry + runtime flags, (2) drew: contract template, (3) sanjay: pricing examples, (4) clare: pilot onboarding doc. Review on Mon 9am PT. Thanks. :white_check_mark:
